audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Arad, bronze serpent, journey stations, well song, and Transjordan battle text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Arad conflict and herem, Edom detour, serpent crisis and bronze-serpent healing sign, travel stations and ancient poems, well song, Sihon and Og battles, and conquest of Amorite territory. Strong anti-colonial, anti-violence, anti-idolatry, and medical-safety safeguards required.

verses.restored: The Canaanite king of Arad, dwelling in Negev, heard that Israel came by way of Atharim; he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.

familiar.text: And when king Arad the Canaanite, which dwelt in the south, heard tell that Israel came by the way of the spies; then he fought against Israel, and took some of them prisoners.

modern.text: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע הַכְּנַעֲנִ֤י מֶֽלֶךְ עֲרָד֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב הַנֶּ֔גֶב כִּ֚י בָּ֣א יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הָאֲתָרִ֑ים וַיִּלָּ֨חֶם֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּ֥שְׁבְּ מִמֶּ֖נּוּ שֶֽׁבִי

verses.restored: Israel vowed a vow to YHWH and said, If giving you give this people into my hand, then I will devote their cities to destruction.

familiar.text: And Israel vowed a vow unto the LORD, and said, If thou wilt indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.

modern.text: So Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If You will deliver this people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction. ”

original.text: וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל נֶ֛דֶר לַֽיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אִם נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֜ן אֶת הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְהַֽחֲרַמְתִּ֖י אֶת עָרֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: YHWH listened to voice of Israel and gave the Canaanite, and they devoted them and their cities; name of place was called Hormah/Devotion.

familiar.text: And the LORD hearkened to the voice of Israel, and delivered up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities: and he called the name of the place Hormah.

modern.text: And the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; so they named the place Hormah. The Bronze Serpent

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע יְהוָ֜ה בְּק֣וֹל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וַיַּחֲרֵ֥ם אֶתְהֶ֖ם וְאֶת עָרֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א שֵׁם הַמָּק֖וֹם חָרְמָֽה

verses.restored: They set out from Mount Hor by way of Sea of Reeds to go around land of Edom, and soul/life of people became short/impatient on way.

familiar.text: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.

modern.text: Then they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the journey

original.text: וַיִּסְע֞וּ מֵהֹ֤ר הָהָר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יַם ס֔וּף לִסְבֹ֖ב אֶת אֶ֣רֶץ אֱד֑וֹם וַתִּקְצַ֥ר נֶֽפֶשׁ הָעָ֖ם בַּדָּֽרֶךְ

verses.restored: The people spoke against Divine and against Moses: Why have you brought us up from Egypt to die in wilderness? For there is no bread and no water, and our soul/life loathes this miserable bread.

familiar.text: And the people spake against God, and against Moses, Wherefore have ye brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? for there is no bread, neither is there any water; and our soul loatheth this light bread.

modern.text: and spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and we detest this wretched food!”

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר הָעָ֗ם בֵּֽאלֹהִים֮ וּבְמֹשֶׁה֒ לָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֨נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לָמ֖וּת בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְאֵ֣ין מַ֔יִם וְנַפְשֵׁ֣נוּ קָ֔צָה בַּלֶּ֖חֶם הַקְּלֹקֵֽל

verses.restored: YHWH sent among people fiery serpents, and they bit people, and many people from Israel died.

familiar.text: And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.

modern.text: So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died.

original.text: וַיְשַׁלַּ֨ח יְהוָ֜ה בָּעָ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַנְּחָשִׁ֣ים הַשְּׂרָפִ֔ים וַֽיְנַשְּׁכ֖וּ אֶת הָעָ֑ם וַיָּ֥מָת עַם רָ֖ב מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: The people came to Moses and said, We have sinned/misaligned, for we spoke against YHWH and against you. Pray to YHWH that he remove serpent from us. Moses prayed for people.

familiar.text: Therefore the people came to Moses, and said, We have sinned, for we have spoken against the LORD, and against thee; pray unto the LORD, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moses prayed for the people.

modern.text: Then the people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us.” So Moses interceded for the people.

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ הָעָ֨ם אֶל מֹשֶׁ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ חָטָ֗אנוּ כִּֽי דִבַּ֤רְנוּ בַֽיהוָה֙ וָבָ֔ךְ הִתְפַּלֵּל֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה וְיָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלֵ֖ינוּ אֶת הַנָּחָ֑שׁ וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֥ל מֹשֶׁ֖ה בְּעַ֥ד הָעָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses, Make for yourself a fiery serpent and put it upon a standard; it shall be that everyone bitten, when he sees it, shall live.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֗ה עֲשֵׂ֤ה לְךָ֙ שָׂרָ֔ף וְשִׂ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ עַל נֵ֑ס וְהָיָה֙ כָּל הַנָּשׁ֔וּךְ וְרָאָ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ וָחָֽי

verses.restored: Moses made a serpent of bronze and put it upon standard; and it was, if serpent bit a man and he looked toward bronze serpent, he lived.

familiar.text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

modern.text: So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live. The Journey to Moab

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ מֹשֶׁה֙ נְחַ֣שׁ נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וַיְשִׂמֵ֖הוּ עַל הַנֵּ֑ס וְהָיָ֗ה אִם נָשַׁ֤ךְ הַנָּחָשׁ֙ אֶת אִ֔ישׁ וְהִבִּ֛יט אֶל נְחַ֥שׁ הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת וָחָֽי

verses.restored: Children of Israel set out and camped at Oboth.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel set forward, and pitched in Oboth.

modern.text: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּאֹבֹֽת

verses.restored: They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in wilderness facing Moab toward sunrise.

familiar.text: And they journeyed from Oboth, and pitched at Ijeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrising.

modern.text: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מֵאֹבֹ֑ת וַֽיַּחֲנ֞וּ בְּעִיֵּ֣י הָֽעֲבָרִ֗ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל פְּנֵ֣י מוֹאָ֔ב מִמִּזְרַ֖ח הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ

verses.restored: From there they set out and camped in wadi Zered.

familiar.text: From thence they removed, and pitched in the valley of Zared.

modern.text: From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.

original.text: מִשָּׁ֖ם נָסָ֑עוּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּנַ֥חַל זָֽרֶד

verses.restored: From there they set out and camped beyond Arnon, which is in wilderness going out from border of Amorites; for Arnon is border of Moab, between Moab and Amorites.

familiar.text: From thence they removed, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, which is in the wilderness that cometh out of the coasts of the Amorites: for Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.

modern.text: From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends into the Amorite territory. Now the Arnon is the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.

original.text: מִשָּׁם֮ נָסָעוּ֒ וַֽיַּחֲנ֗וּ מֵעֵ֤בֶר אַרְנוֹן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר הַיֹּצֵ֖א מִגְּב֣וּל הָֽאֱמֹרִ֑י כִּ֤י אַרְנוֹן֙ גְּב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב בֵּ֥ין מוֹאָ֖ב וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי

verses.restored: Therefore it is said in Book of Wars of YHWH: Waheb in Suphah, and wadis of Arnon,

familiar.text: Wherefore it is said in the book of the wars of the LORD, What he did in the Red sea, and in the brooks of Arnon,

modern.text: Therefore it is stated in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon,

original.text: עַל כֵּן֙ יֵֽאָמַ֔ר בְּסֵ֖פֶר מִלְחֲמֹ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אֶת וָהֵ֣ב בְּסוּפָ֔ה וְאֶת הַנְּחָלִ֖ים אַרְנֽוֹן

verses.restored: and slope of wadis that turns toward dwelling of Ar and leans upon border of Moab.

familiar.text: And at the stream of the brooks that goeth down to the dwelling of Ar, and lieth upon the border of Moab.

modern.text: even the slopes of the wadis that extend to the site of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.”

original.text: וְאֶ֨שֶׁד֙ הַנְּחָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָ֖ה לְשֶׁ֣בֶת עָ֑ר וְנִשְׁעַ֖ן לִגְב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: From there to Beer/Well; that is well where YHWH said to Moses, Gather people, and I will give them water.

familiar.text: And from thence they went to Beer: that is the well whereof the LORD spake unto Moses, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.

modern.text: From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people so that I may give them water.”

original.text: וּמִשָּׁ֖ם בְּאֵ֑רָה הִ֣וא הַבְּאֵ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ לְמֹשֶׁ֔ה אֱסֹף֙ אֶת הָעָ֔ם וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם מָֽיִם

verses.restored: Then Israel sang this song: Rise up, well! Answer to it!

familiar.text: Then Israel sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it:

modern.text: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!

original.text: אָ֚ז יָשִׁ֣יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת הַשִּׁירָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את עֲלִ֥י בְאֵ֖ר עֱנוּ לָֽהּ

verses.restored: Well that leaders dug, that nobles of people excavated, with scepter, with their staffs. And from wilderness to Mattanah,

familiar.text: The princes digged the well, the nobles of the people digged it, by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves. And from the wilderness they went to Mattanah:

modern.text: The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs.” From the wilderness the Israelites went on to Mattanah,

original.text: בְּאֵ֞ר חֲפָר֣וּהָ שָׂרִ֗ים כָּר֨וּהָ֙ נְדִיבֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם בִּמְחֹקֵ֖ק בְּמִשְׁעֲנֹתָ֑ם וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר מַתָּנָֽה

verses.restored: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

familiar.text: And from Mattanah to Nahaliel: and from Nahaliel to Bamoth:

modern.text: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,

original.text: וּמִמַּתָּנָ֖ה נַחֲלִיאֵ֑ל וּמִנַּחֲלִיאֵ֖ל בָּמֽוֹת

verses.restored: and from Bamoth to valley that is in field of Moab, at top of Pisgah, overlooking face of wasteland.

familiar.text: And from Bamoth in the valley, that is in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looketh toward Jeshimon.

modern.text: and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. The Defeat of Sihon (Deuteronomy 2:24–37)

original.text: וּמִבָּמ֗וֹת הַגַּיְא֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בִּשְׂדֵ֣ה מוֹאָ֔ב רֹ֖אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֑ה וְנִשְׁקָ֖פָה עַל פְּנֵ֥י הַיְשִׁימֹֽן

verses.restored: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of Amorites, saying,

familiar.text: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

modern.text: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל סִיחֹ֥ן מֶֽלֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Let me pass through your land. We will not turn into field or vineyard; we will not drink water of well; by king's road we will go until we pass through your border.

familiar.text: Let me pass through thy land: we will not turn into the fields, or into the vineyards; we will not drink of the waters of the well: but we will go along by the king’s high way, until we be past thy borders.

modern.text: “Let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”

original.text: אֶעְבְּרָ֣ה בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם לֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבֻלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Sihon did not allow Israel to pass through his border; Sihon gathered all his people and went out to meet Israel in wilderness, and came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.

familiar.text: And Sihon would not suffer Israel to pass through his border: but Sihon gathered all his people together, and went out against Israel into the wilderness: and he came to Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

modern.text: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness. When he came to Jahaz, he fought against Israel.

original.text: וְלֹא נָתַ֨ן סִיחֹ֣ן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻלוֹ֒ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֨ף סִיחֹ֜ן אֶת כָּל עַמּ֗וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֞א לִקְרַ֤את יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּדְבָּ֔רָה וַיָּבֹ֖א יָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Israel struck him by edge of sword and possessed his land from Arnon to Jabbok, as far as children of Ammon, for border of children of Ammon was strong.

familiar.text: And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.

modern.text: And Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok—but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified.

original.text: וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְפִי חָ֑רֶב וַיִּירַ֨שׁ אֶת אַרְצ֜וֹ מֵֽאַרְנֹ֗ן עַד יַבֹּק֙ עַד בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן כִּ֣י עַ֔ז גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן

verses.restored: Israel took all these cities, and Israel dwelt in all cities of Amorites, in Heshbon and all its daughters.

familiar.text: And Israel took all these cities: and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.

modern.text: Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites and occupied them, including Heshbon and all its villages.

original.text: וַיִּקַּח֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ת כָּל הֶעָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּכָל עָרֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י בְּחֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן וּבְכָל בְּנֹתֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: For Heshbon was city of Sihon king of Amorites, and he had fought against former king of Moab and taken all his land from his hand as far as Arnon.

familiar.text: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab, and taken all his land out of his hand, even unto Arnon.

modern.text: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.

original.text: כִּ֣י חֶשְׁבּ֔וֹן עִ֗יר סִיחֹ֛ן מֶ֥לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֖י הִ֑וא וְה֣וּא נִלְחַ֗ם בְּמֶ֤לֶךְ מוֹאָב֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן וַיִּקַּ֧ח אֶת כָּל אַרְצ֛וֹ מִיָּד֖וֹ עַד אַרְנֹֽן

verses.restored: Therefore the proverb-makers say: Come to Heshbon; let city of Sihon be built and established.

familiar.text: Wherefore they that speak in proverbs say, Come into Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and prepared:

modern.text: That is why the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored.

original.text: עַל כֵּ֛ן יֹאמְר֥וּ הַמֹּשְׁלִ֖ים בֹּ֣אוּ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן תִּבָּנֶ֥ה וְתִכּוֹנֵ֖ן עִ֥יר סִיחֽוֹן

modern.text: For a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon’s heights.

modern.text: Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as refugees, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.

modern.text: Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet them in battle at Edrei.

original.text: וַיִּפְנוּ֙ וַֽיַּעֲל֔וּ דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתָ֜ם ה֧וּא וְכָל עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand, and all his people, and his land; and thou shalt do to him as thou didst unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.

modern.text: But the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”

verses.restored: They struck him and his sons and all his people until no survivor remained to him, and they possessed his land.

familiar.text: So they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him alive: and they possessed his land.

modern.text: So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land.

original.text: וַיַּכּ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ וְאֶת בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת כָּל עַמּ֔וֹ עַד בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר ל֖וֹ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיִּֽירְשׁ֖וּ אֶת אַרְצֽוֹ

translation_notes: The Arad vow and destruction language is herem warfare material and must not be used to justify modern annihilation, ethnic cleansing, or sacred violence.
Israel goes around Edom rather than violating Edom's refusal from chapter 20.

The bronze serpent is a narrative healing sign in response to a serpent crisis; it is not permission for snake handling, magical medicine, or rejection of healthcare. Later tradition records its destruction when it became an object of worship.
The well song preserves communal gratitude and may reflect shared labor by leaders and people.
The chapter includes ancient war poetry celebrating Sihon's conquest of Moab before Israel's conquest of Sihon; these layered voices require literary and historical audit.
Sihon and Og narratives preserve territorial warfare and totalizing victory rhetoric. They must not be mapped onto modern peoples or borders.
Requests for passage do not erase the sovereignty or humanity of peoples already inhabiting the land.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 21 to sanctify genocide, territorial conquest, forced displacement, snake handling, magical healing, or refusal of medical care. Preserve the ancient conflict narrative while clearly rejecting modern violence and centering water, healing, route boundaries, and the humanity of every people named.
